fhb-low-deposit.html: Buying a first home without a full 20% deposit is more common than many buyers expect. In September 2026, just over half of all first-home mortgages approved across New Zealand (50.3%—1,342 of 2,667 loans, or $850m in lending) went to buyers with under a 20% deposit, up from 46.0% a year earlier.
fhb-low-deposit.source_html: Source: RBNZ Table C31, © Reserve Bank of New Zealand. Percentages & averages derived by HLF. Historical market statistics for general information only, not personalised financial advice.
fhb-low-deposit.name: First-home buyers with less than 20% deposit
fhb-low-deposit.source: Reserve Bank of New Zealand Table C31
fhb-low-deposit.data_type: HLF-derived share & HLF-calculated comparison (from officially reported RBNZ loan counts & dollar values)
fhb-low-deposit.definition: The percentage of firm residential mortgage commitments to New Zealand first-home buyers where the Loan-to-Value Ratio (LVR) exceeds 80% (meaning the buyer has less than a 20% deposit), measured by borrower/loan count alongside officially reported high-LVR dollar lending.
fhb-low-deposit.methodology: Compiled from monthly registered bank returns under RBNZ Table C31. First-home buyers are defined by lending banks as borrowers purchasing a residential property to occupy as a first home.
fhb-low-deposit.hlf_calculation: (High-LVR FHB Borrowers [LVRN.MMB2.BC1] / Total FHB Borrowers [LVRN.MMB2.AC1]) * 100, compared against the same month 12 months earlier.
fhb-low-deposit.summary_text: Buying a first home without a full 20% deposit is more common than many buyers expect. In September 2026, just over half of all first-home mortgages approved across New Zealand (50.3%—1,342 of 2,667 loans, or $850m in lending) went to buyers with under a 20% deposit, up from 46.0% a year earlier.

fhb-share.html: First-home buyers continue to make up an active slice of the New Zealand market—in September 2026, banks approved 2,667 first-home mortgages (20.3% of all new mortgage lending, up from 19.2% a year earlier), with an average loan size of $574k.
fhb-share.source_html: Source: RBNZ Table C31, © Reserve Bank of New Zealand. Percentages & averages derived by HLF. Historical market statistics for general information only, not personalised financial advice.
fhb-share.name: First-home buyer share of total New Zealand mortgage lending
fhb-share.source: Reserve Bank of New Zealand Table C31
fhb-share.data_type: Officially reported loan count & HLF-derived market share / average loan size
fhb-share.definition: The proportion of total new residential mortgage lending dollars in New Zealand committed to first-home buyers, alongside the officially reported monthly count of approved first-home loans and HLF-derived average loan size.
fhb-share.methodology: Sourced from RBNZ Table C31 monthly registered bank commitments across first-home buyers, other owner-occupiers, property investors, and business purposes.
fhb-share.hlf_calculation: Share = (FHB Lending NZDm [LVRN.MMB1.AC1] / Total Lending NZDm [LVRN.MMB1.AA]) * 100. Avg Loan = (LVRN.MMB1.AC1 * 1,000,000) / LVRN.MMB2.AC1.
fhb-share.summary_text: First-home buyers continue to make up an active slice of the New Zealand market—in September 2026, banks approved 2,667 first-home mortgages (20.3% of all new mortgage lending, up from 19.2% a year earlier), with an average loan size of $574k.

investors.hlf_calculation: Investor Share = (Investor Lending NZDm [LVRN.MMB1.AN] / All Borrower Lending NZDm [LVRN.MMB1.AA]) * 100.
investors.summary_text: First-home buyers are currently borrowing more overall than property investors—in September 2026, investors made up 17.7% of new mortgage lending ($1.33B, down from 21.2% a year earlier), compared with 20.3% for first-home buyers.

refinance.definition: The monthly number of borrowers and total dollar value of residential mortgages switching from one mortgage provider to another in New Zealand.

refinance.hlf_calculation: Share = (Refinance NZDm [LVRN.MMB1.AZD] / Total Purpose Lending NZDm) * 100. Avg Refinance Loan = (LVRN.MMB1.AZD * 1,000,000) / LVRN.MMB2.AZD.
refinance.summary_text: Moving banks is a regular part of the New Zealand mortgage market rather than a rare step—in September 2026 alone, 2,772 borrowers switched mortgage providers, moving $1.73B in loans (23.0% of all new lending, at an average loan size of $624k).

top-ups.summary_text: Many Kiwi homeowners tap into existing equity for renovations or upgrades rather than moving house—in September 2026, 9,639 borrowers topped up an existing mortgage, making up 46.4% of all mortgage approvals by count (average top-up: $100k).

kiwisaver-first-home.definition: The monthly number of KiwiSaver members withdrawing funds to purchase a first home, total dollars withdrawn, and HLF-derived average withdrawal per member and per approved first-home mortgage.

investor-low-deposit.html: Even for property investors, low-deposit approvals happen every month through new-build exemptions and bank speed limits. In September 2026, New Zealand banks approved 52 investor mortgages ($36m, or 1.9% of investors) with strictly under a 20% deposit (>80% LVR)—up from 34 loans ($23m) a year earlier (and 508 loans / $328m over the past 12 months)—plus another 475 investor loans ($301m, or 17.8%) in the 20%–30% deposit tier (70%–80% LVR) where standard 20%-deposit new-build investment loans sit.

investor-low-deposit.methodology: In RBNZ Table C31, strictly under-20% deposit investor loans are recorded in >80% LVR (LVRN.MMB2.BN / LVRN.MMB1.BN), while exact 20.0% deposit (80.0% LVR) new-build investor loans sit inside 70% < LVR <= 80% (LVRN.MMB2.DN minus LVRN.MMB2.BN).

investor-new-build-lvr.definition: The total number, dollar value, and percentage share of New Zealand property investor mortgages approved with under a 30% deposit (>70% LVR), capturing 20%-deposit new-build exemptions and bank speed-limit allocations.
investor-new-build-lvr.methodology: Sourced from RBNZ Table C31 Memo Item H2/D2 (Higher than 70% LVR investor borrowers and lending).
investor-new-build-lvr.hlf_calculation: Share = (LVRN.MMB2.DN / LVRN.MMB2.AN) * 100; split into 70%–80% LVR and >80% LVR tiers.
investor-new-build-lvr.summary_text: Because brand-new builds are exempt from Reserve Bank LVR restrictions, nearly one in five property investors buys with less than the standard 30% existing-property deposit. In September 2026, 527 investor loans ($337m, or 19.8% of investor approvals) were approved with under a 30% deposit (>70% LVR)—comprising 475 loans ($301m) in the 20%–30% deposit band (which includes 20%-deposit new builds) and 52 loans ($36m) with under a 20% deposit (>80% LVR).
